limitations: Calibration evidence comes from a CLEAN-ISH reference built from your own data (complete rows, no duplicates, wild target values removed), random injected errors, a Random Forest regressor and R-squared: 'no harm observed' means none in those runs, not a guarantee.

Estimate-based audit: for an uploaded dataset the true error locations are unknown, so every rate comes from a detector with limited precision and recall. A flagged rate is not a confirmed error rate.

Regression (Phase 21): the wrong-target detector flags target values whose out-of-fold residual is more than 4 robust sigmas from the typical residual (scaled within bands of the predicted value). It finds gross errors, not subtle ones, and it can flag genuine extreme values. On a clean reference it flagged under 2% of rows; its precision and recall on injected errors are in docs/PHASE21_SPEC.md. Its replacement value is a model prediction, so it is never applied automatically without evidence from your own data.

There is no regression benchmark behind the default policy: unless the calibration is run on your data, no repair is applied automatically and no impact estimate is shown. The Adult evidence is classification-only and is not used.

No before/after model metrics are reported in the audit itself: an uploaded dataset has no clean held-out test set. The model panel compares models on held-out rows that are as dirty as your file, so a gain there does not prove a repair was right.

Duplicates are full-record duplicates (features + target). Placeholder tokens ('?', 'N/A', '-', empty, ...) are counted as missing in the analysis; a token that is a genuine category in your data will be over-counted as missing.
Files above the model-detector row limit are audited on a sample (stratified by target quintile) for the target and feature detectors; their findings and proposals then cover only the sampled rows.
The 'aggressive' variant applies every proposed repair except feature-anomaly repairs; with no calibration no repair in it is certified safe.

leakage.note: Test rows that also appear (all columns identical) in the training rows. They inflate the 'before' score; 'score_noleak_mean' scores only the rows with no copy.

panel.caveat: This compares models trained on your raw rows with models trained on the repaired rows, scored on the same untouched held-out rows, which are as dirty as your file. A gain means the repaired training rows predicted the real rows better; it does not prove each repair was correct, and a loss can mean the held-out targets are noisy. Changes smaller than the noise floor are labelled 'within noise'.
